claims.text: The formation and stability of a protective iron oxide film governs the corrosion resistance of as-received Q235 steel.
At room temperature, the oxide layer on Q235 steel remains intact and provides corrosion protection.
During aggressive salt exposure at 700–900 °C, localized microstructural features mediate disruption or transformation of the oxide layer.
Disruption or transformation of the oxide layer at high temperature increases corrosion degradation.
As-received Q235 steel contains inherent microstructural heterogeneities relevant to its corrosion behavior.
Grain boundaries and inclusions influence the nucleation and stability of the protective iron oxide film.
At lower temperatures, a coherent and continuous iron oxide film forms on Q235 steel.
A coherent and continuous iron oxide film acts as a passive barrier against corrosion.
High temperature and aggressive salt species disrupt the oxide film preferentially at microstructural weak points.
Preferential oxide-film disruption leads to localized corrosion and loss of protection.
Room-temperature exposure will produce a continuous oxide film and minimal corrosion.
High-temperature chloride-salt exposure will produce measurable oxide-layer disruption relative to unexposed reference specimens.
High-temperature chloride-salt exposure will produce deeper corrosion pits and greater mass loss than the reference condition.
The native oxide film remains undisturbed when Q235 steel is not exposed to aggressive salt or high temperature.
Homogenizing annealing reduces the microstructural heterogeneities implicated in oxide-film disruption.
Similar high-temperature oxide integrity and corrosion behavior in as-received and homogenized specimens would falsify the proposed role of localized microstructural features.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to alloyed, annealed, specially treated, or high-entropy-alloy materials because their protective mechanisms may differ.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that temperature and salt presence/absence are the only variables, whereas the falsification study additionally varies material state through homogenizing annealing.
